The only filters we've used for many years now. We have a Cuisinart coffee maker that automatically grinds the coffee just before brewing. We also like it strong so there is a lot of coffee in the basket. When we used other products, the ground would end up going over the filter and into the carafe making the coffee a tad bit crunchy. Since these are taller, they eliminate that issue. I haven't seen them in the stores, but buying in bulk on Amazon is easy and super cheap. If you get grounds in your coffee at home you may want to give these a try.
Tip-If your coffee maker has a cover for the basket, make sure you don't push the edge of the filter down when you put it on. Since these are taller, it's easy to make that mistake. That will probably make more sense to Cuisinart coffee maker owners.

Bunn filters are not the least expensive filters you can buy, but they are the best. Most coffee filters on the market are shorter and don’t reach the top of the basket allowing some coffees, as they are brewing, to overflow the filter and basket spilling grounds into the carafe. These filters also filter fast and at the same time also catch the oil that naturally comes from coffee, that means little chance of heartburn that you might get from other filters that don’t catch the oil. The only thing, like many filters out there, they can be hard to peel apart, just takes a little patience.

This is probably one of the best investments I could have ever made, I say that because I live in a small apartment and it fit perfectly in a corner of my kitchen.  I usually would spend about 20 - 30 dollars a week in the laundry mat and it was a drag to carry loads and bring them back to the third floor. So when I saw this machine I just had to get it because this way Im doing laundry in my own home even though it is a bit of hands on work but well worth it. I had a bit of problems with the draining but I figured out that the hose has to be at a low level to clean out, so I put it to drain in the bathtub because I use the bathroom to do the laundry.  I use the hose that fits in the back of the machine to fill the tub and after I fill the tub I switch the hose to the spinner and I turn the water and give it  the first minute  to spin the soapy water oit and another minute while the water is running and that is where I add the softener and let that ru. For another minute then I turn. Off the water and reset it to spin all the way. The clothes are spin dry , clean and smelling good. I even bought a clothes rack to dry the clothes off. So far I have saved over 100 dollars. Love this machine and I even tried to look for a bigger machine but had no luck.
